bio:
Andrew Humphrey Heffernan was baptized at Killenaule, County Tipperary, on 3 April 1842, the son of Thomas Heffernan and Catherine Boney of Mardyke, a colliery townland in the Slieveardagh coalfield. The birth date of 31 March 1848 that his obituary and some later records give is wrong, since his sister Catherine was baptized in February 1848. His father died in Ireland, and Andrew came to America "when very young" with his mother and brothers, some time between about 1861 and 1866, settling at Larksville in Luzerne County, Pennsylvania; he later became a naturalized citizen.

On 1 September 1868 he married Mary Connole at Plymouth. Mary's stepmother, Anastasia Boney Connole, was the widow of Andrew's uncle Richard Heffernan, which probably explains how the couple met. Fifty years later, in September 1918, the Sunday Independent marked their anniversary with a piece headed "Married Fifty Years". Mary, born in New York in November 1850, bore eleven children, ten of whom lived; the family produced newspapermen and an Army aviator. In 1900 the household at Plymouth Borough still held Thomas, 29, a newspaper reporter, Norah, 26, a dressmaker, Annie, 23, a tailoress, Mary, 21, Andrew, 19, Josephine, 16, and John, 13.

Andrew was not a miner. He was a school janitor in 1900, a clerk in 1914, and, in the words of his obituary, "an attache of the Court house in various capacities". He died at Wilkes-Barre on 6 May 1919. The records disagree on his resting place: his death certificate gives burial at St. Vincent's, Plymouth, on 9 May 1919, which places him in St. Vincent DePaul Cemetery at Larksville, while a family history notes a tombstone for him at St. Mary's in Hanover Township. He is John's 3rd-great-grandfather.
funFacts: The Heffernans mined anthracite in Tipperary's Slieveardagh field before the family came to the Pennsylvania anthracite field.
His wife's stepmother was also his aunt.

researchNotes:
Andrew Humphrey Heffernan was baptized at Killenaule, Co. Tipperary, on 3 Apr 1842, son of Thomas Heffernan and Catherine Boney 'of Mardyke' (a colliery townland in the Slieveardagh coalfield). The tree, his obituary and a FamilySearch profile give a birth of 31 Mar 1848, which is wrong (his sister Catherine was baptized Feb 1848); Harvey & Smith's 'died in 1919 at the age of seventy-six' fits c.1843. His father died in Ireland, and his obituary says he came to America 'when very young' with 'his mother and brothers' and settled in Larksville; his brother John's obituary and the 1900 census put that arrival about 1864-66, while Harvey says 'about 1861'. On 1 Sep 1868 he married Mary Connole at Plymouth (a 1 Sep 1918 Sunday Independent piece was headed 'Married Fifty Years'). Mary's stepmother Anastasia (Boney) Connole was his own aunt by marriage (widow of his father's brother Richard), which probably explains how the couple met. His obituary describes him as 'an attache of the Court house in various capacities', not a miner, and mentions no Civil War service. In 1914 his son's Philadelphia marriage application described him as a clerk born in Ireland. They had ten surviving children. He died at Wilkes-Barre on 6 May 1919 (PA death certificate dated 8 May 1919, cited by Dwyer); Harvey vol. V's 'died in 1912' is an error. The death certificate gives burial at St. Vincent's, Plymouth, on 9 May 1919, the deep-dive report places him in St. Vincent DePaul Cemetery, Larksville (Find a Grave 139403710), and Dwyer notes his tombstone is in St. Mary's, Hanover Twp.

The state death index for 1919 has "Hefferman, Andrew; 61616; Wilkes Barre; May 6" ([R4-S1]), confirming the date Dwyer took from the certificate. In the 1900 census of Plymouth Borough, Ward 3 ([R4-S2]) Andrew, 53, gave his birth as March 1847 in Ireland, immigration in 1863, and occupation school janitor; Mary, 49, born Nov 1850 in New York, had borne 11 children, 10 living. At home were Thomas (29, newspaper reporter), Norah (26, dressmaker), Annie (23, tailoress), Mary (21), Andrew (19), Josephine (16) and John (13). The "11 born, 10 living" count implies one child who died young, matching an unnamed "Daughter Heffernan" on FamilySearch.
